messages.author: e7a71d967e60bb41
messages.subject: Size of lines in point
parts:
Dear All,
Consider the snippet at the end of the email.
By increasing the size parameter in geom_point, I can get a larger
triangle but what if I want just to increase the thickness of the lines
constituting the triangle symbol itself without magnifying it? Is that
doable in ggplot2?
Cheers

Lorenzo


########################################

library(ggplot2)


my_data <- cbind(as.data.frame(seq(5)),as.data.frame(seq(5)))

names(my_data) <- c("frame1", "frame2")


gpl <- ggplot(data=my_data)+
geom_point(aes(x=frame1,y=frame2), size=4, shape=2, col="red")


pdf("point_fig.pdf")
print(gpl)
dev.off()

> No, because there is no control at the R level.  You could however

That's certainly the best option. Only for your curiosity, I'll
mention an *experimental* geom to draw little polygons instead of the
base R shapes, so you can do,

library(ggExtra) # r-forge
ggplot(data=my_data) +
geom_ngon(aes(x=frame1,y=frame2), sides=3, size=4, angle=-pi/6,
col="red", lex=4)

but I wouldn't recommend using it in anything serious.


baptiste

I see, but I am experiencing problems in implementing this simple
suggestion in the following example.
Most likely, I am misunderstanding something.
Here I want to make a plot with lines and points and have the composite
symbol (line+point) in the legend.
It is almost OK, but I am not able to control the filling state of the
points.
I am sure the solution must be a one-liner, can anyone point me in the
right direction?
Cheers

Lorenzo



#####################################


require(ggplot2)


x <- data.frame(x_val=c(seq(5),seq(5) ))
y <- data.frame(y_val=seq(5), case="A")
y2 <- data.frame(y_val=2*seq(5), case="B")

dat <- rbind(y, y2)
all_data <- cbind(x,dat)

lbls <- levels(all_data$case)

gpl <- ggplot(all_data, aes(x=x_val, y=y_val, color=case, shape=case))+
geom_point(size=2, fill="red")+
geom_point(size=4)+
geom_line()+
scale_shape_manual("Network", breaks=lbls, labels=lbls, values=c(1,2)) +
scale_colour_manual("Network", breaks=lbls, labels=lbls, values=c(1,2))
#scale_fill_manual("Network", breaks=lbls, labels=lbls, values=c(1,2))

fn <- paste("hollow.pdf")

pdf(fn)

print(gpl)
dev.off()

--

There is still one thing I do not get. See the snippet at the end of the
email.
Whenever I try to set my own shapes/colours, then the filling of the
symbols gets lots.
In hadley-hollow.pdf I correctly have the white color within each
triangle/circle, but that is not the case in hollow.pdf.
Why is that? In other words: can I combine manual shape and colour
scales with filled symbols?
Cheers

Lorenzo
################################
################################

library(ggplot2)


rm(list=ls())

x <- data.frame(x_val=c(seq(5),seq(5) ))
y <- data.frame(y_val=seq(5), case="A")
y2 <- data.frame(y_val=2*seq(5), case="B")

dat <- rbind(y, y2)
all_data <- cbind(x,dat)

lbls <- levels(all_data$case)

gpl <- ggplot(all_data, aes(x=x_val, y=y_val,color=case, shape=case))+
geom_point(size=4)+
geom_point(colour="white", size = 2)+
scale_shape(solid = TRUE)+

geom_line()+
scale_shape_manual("Network", breaks=lbls, labels=lbls, values=c(1,2)) +
scale_colour_manual("Network", breaks=lbls, labels=lbls, values=c(1,2))
#scale_fill_manual("Network", breaks=lbls, labels=lbls, values=c(1,2))



fn <- paste("hollow.pdf")

pdf(fn)
print(gpl)
dev.off()

had <- ggplot(all_data, aes(x=x_val, y=y_val,color=case, shape=case))+
geom_point(size=4)+
geom_line()+
geom_point(colour="white", size = 2)+
scale_shape(solid = TRUE)

fn <- paste("hadley-hollow.pdf")

pdf(fn)
print(had)
dev.off()

messages.subject: Re: Size of lines in point
parts:
Hi,

If you use scale_shape_manual, you need to select shapes that have a
fill value (that was done automatically by scale_shape(solid=TRUE).
For instance,

ggplot(all_data, aes(x=x_val, y=y_val, color=case, shape=case, fill=case))+
geom_point(size=4)+
geom_point(size=2, fill="white")+
geom_line()+
scale_shape_manual("Network", breaks=lbls, labels=lbls, values=c(21, 24)) +
scale_colour_manual("Network", breaks=lbls, labels=lbls, values=c(1,2)) +
scale_fill_manual("Network", breaks=lbls, labels=lbls, values=c(1,2))


HTH,

baptiste
